entry.title: Add in-app vocabulary review
entry.content:
Add in-app vocabulary review

Words are scheduled with the same FSRS the handwriting loop uses, with a
recognition prompt, the mined sentence on the answer, and keyboard
shortcuts. The calendar counts reviews and the home panel surfaces what
is due.

This reverses the earlier position that vocabulary belonged only in Anki.
That held while the app had nothing Anki lacked; with mining, handwriting
checking and the kanji-word links, requiring Anki became a limitation.
Export stays one-way and optional, and the two are not synced.

entry.title: Add Anki export
entry.content:
Add Anki export

Collection exports vocabulary as a real .apkg via exporter/build_apkg.py,
with a plain-text fallback that needs no Python. Notes carry the sentence
each word was mined from, over Recognition and Recall templates.

GUIDs key on vocab_item.id, so re-exporting updates existing cards and
preserves review history. The note type uses its own model id, distinct
from the separate 日本語 Anki Decks pipeline's.

A script rather than a service: exports are occasional, so there is
nothing to gain from a second process holding a port.

entry.title: Show your own history on the kanji page
entry.content:
Show your own history on the kanji page

The page was a dictionary entry; it now also shows what is true of you.
Saved words containing the character with the sentences they came from,
your practice tally, when it next comes up, and other kanji in your
library sharing components — ranked by how many, since one shared 木
links hundreds of characters and means little.

All four ratings are carried so the tallies reconcile: a Hard fell into
neither the failed nor the right bucket and made the numbers look wrong.

entry.title: Show recently viewed kanji in the chip row
entry.content:
Show recently viewed kanji in the chip row

The five chips now lead with characters you have actually looked up,
most recent first, padded with the original examples so the row is never
empty — without a Japanese IME those chips are the only way into the
page.

Only successful lookups are recorded, so a character with no dictionary
entry never lands there. Kept in localStorage: recently viewed is
per-device by nature, and a server round trip would make the row flicker
in on every load.

entry.title: Fix Japanese input on the kanji page
entry.content:
Fix Japanese input on the kanji page

The lookup field read its value from the URL, so every keystroke
navigated and overwrote the field. That made IME composition impossible —
typing "yama" was destroyed after the first letter — and backspacing to
empty navigated home.

The field now holds its own text and commits to the URL on change, or on
compositionend while an IME is active. Clearing goes to /kanji rather
than /, so backspace no longer throws you off the page.

entry.title: Fix page sizing for desktop screens
entry.content:
Fix page sizing for desktop screens

The 62rem page cap was a reading measure applied to an app: at 1920 the
kanji, mining, collection and practice pages used 54% of the screen.
Pages now fill to 1600px while text keeps its own measure.

Kanji sections flow into columns, collection words go multi-column,
mining puts the word detail beside the passage, and practice fits
prompt, canvas and answer in one row. The drawing canvas grows to 420px
where there is room.

Grid minimums use min(…, 100%) so tracks can collapse on narrow screens
— minmax(29rem, 1fr) was forcing horizontal overflow on mobile.

entry.title: Show mined words in the collection
entry.content:
Show mined words in the collection

Collection splits into Words and Kanji tabs.
Each saved word shows its
reading, meaning and the sentence it was mined from, and any kanji in the
term links to its own page — so a word is a route into its characters.
Both lists can be removed from.

entry.title: Number the user's own strokes on reveal
entry.content:
Number the user's own strokes on reveal

Each drawn stroke is labelled at its start point in draw order, in the
same accent KanjiVG uses, so the two numberings can be compared directly.
Labels offset backwards along the stroke direction to stay off the ink,
with a halo so they remain readable where they overlap.

entry.title: Add study tasks to the home page
entry.content:
Add study tasks to the home page

Two kinds. Suggestions are computed from the library and review tables
"4 due", "2 keep catching you out" and are never stored, so they
resolve themselves rather than needing to be ticked off. Tasks are
user-written and can carry a date and a set of kanji.

Integrated with the calendar in both directions: dated tasks show as
chips on their day, and clicking a day filters the panel and seeds the
add form.

entry.title: Add handwriting practice with FSRS scheduling
entry.content:
Add handwriting practice with FSRS scheduling

Kanji library per user, and a practice session: prompt with meaning plus
both readings, draw on a pointer-event canvas, reveal the numbered
KanjiVG reference, then self-rate. Ratings feed FSRS, which schedules
when each character comes back.

Scheduling is scoped to handwriting deliberately — Anki cannot check
handwriting, so those reviews have nowhere else to live. Vocabulary
reviews stay in Anki.

Strokes are stored normalised to 0..1 so they can later be compared
against KanjiVG's coordinate space for automatic stroke-order checking.

entry.title: Add routing so kanji pages have URLs
entry.content:
Add routing so kanji pages have URLs

/kanji/待 is now a real, linkable page. Chips are links, typing replaces
rather than pushes history, and a multi-character URL canonicalises to
its first character.

entry.title: Add kanji lookup
entry.content:
Add kanji lookup

Import KANJIDIC2 and KanjiVG into Postgres with a one-off runner
(--import-kanji): 10,384 characters, 6,413 stroke-order diagrams.

GET /api/kanji/{literal} returns readings, meanings, grade, JLPT level
and the stroke-order SVG, and the frontend renders it.

Removes the ping scaffolding this replaces.
